standard.title: Rehearse and perform dance
standard.description: rehearse and perform dance for audiences, using technical and expressive skills and, as appropriate genre- or style-specific techniques
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can perform dance with basic technical and expressive skill for an audience (AC9ADA6P01). They have not yet used deliberate rehearsal strategies, production elements, or audience communication tools to enhance the performance experience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students rehearse and perform dance for audiences using deliberate rehearsal strategies, appropriate technical and expressive skills, and production elements to communicate choreographic intent.

nodes.label: Using rehearsal strategies to prepare for performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use deliberate rehearsal strategies to develop confidence, clarity and expressive quality in preparation for performance
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one rehearsal strategy (e.g. spotting, spatial planning, repetition of key phrases) with a specific preparation goal; explain what the strategy helped develop
nodes.typical_width: Use a range of rehearsal strategies to develop confidence, clarity of movement, projection, focus and musicality; document how rehearsal strategies address specific performance challenges
wider: Use video review during rehearsal to identify and address spatial placement, articulation and expressive clarity — compare video observation with own sense of the performance
Plan effective use of available performance spaces during rehearsals — evaluate how spatial planning changes performer confidence and audience experience
Develop a personal rehearsal protocol for preparing a specific aspect of performance (e.g. projection, focus, musicality) — evaluate its effectiveness over multiple rehearsal sessions

response_modes.reason: Effective rehearsal — using targeted strategies repeatedly to address specific performance challenges — is a disciplined habit that develops through sustained practice cycles. Students who rehearse without strategy develop performance confidence more slowly and less deliberately. The skill is in the purposeful application of rehearsal strategies, which develops through iteration.

success_criteria: Uses at least one deliberate rehearsal strategy with a specific goal
Explains what the strategy helped develop
Rehearsal strategy is targeted — not just 'run it again from the top'

nodes.label: Using production elements to communicate intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use production elements to extend communication of choreographic intent to an audience beyond the movement alone
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one production element (projection, soundscape, voice-over, special effects) that could enhance the dance's communication; explain what it would add
nodes.typical_width: Use at least one production element to share key ideas or information about the creative intention of the dance with the audience; evaluate whether the production choice enhances the communication
wider: Develop a production design that uses multiple elements (sound, projection, spatial effects) in coordinated ways — evaluate how each element contributes to the total communicative experience
Investigate how production elements in contemporary professional dance works create meaning beyond the movement — use findings to inform own production decisions
Evaluate the difference between production elements that enhance and those that distract from choreographic intent — develop criteria for purposeful production choice

response_modes.reason: Students commonly add production elements for visual interest without reasoning through whether they enhance or distract from choreographic intent. Scaffolding the reasoning (what does this production choice add, does it serve the choreographic idea, what would the dance communicate without it?) builds purposeful production thinking rather than decoration.

success_criteria: Identifies or uses at least one production element with a communicative purpose
Explains what the element adds to the communication of choreographic intent
Production choice is purposeful — connected to intent, not just visual interest

nodes.label: Performing and communicating with audiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform dance for an audience using technical and expressive skills appropriately, and communicate the choreographic intent through introduction and presentation
nodes.minimum_width: Perform a dance for an audience with at least one deliberate technical and expressive choice; introduce the dance with basic contextual information
nodes.typical_width: Perform dance using technical and expressive skills that serve choreographic intent; introduce the dance using style-specific terminology that communicates the creative intention to the audience
wider: Develop a program note or voice-over introduction using style-specific dance terminology that communicates choreographic intent to an audience unfamiliar with the dance context
Evaluate the performance experience from the audience's perspective — use peer feedback to assess whether the technical and expressive application communicated the intended ideas
Perform the same dance in two different performance contexts (e.g. studio showing vs formal stage) — evaluate how context changes performance choices and audience experience

response_modes.reason: This node integrates rehearsal strategy (Node 1), production elements (Node 2), and technical and expressive skills from C02 into a complete performance event. The coordination of movement, production, and audience communication is the learning — students who can perform technically but cannot communicate with an audience have not met the standard's full demand.

success_criteria: Performs dance with deliberate technical and expressive choices
Introduces the dance in a way that communicates choreographic intent to the audience
Performance is for the audience — not just an execution of choreography
